sentences.text: Shri Akhalesh Gupta, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Dhruv Agrawal, learned counsel for respondent No. 3.

ORDER Appellant/claimant has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the award dated 12/9/2023 passed by Second Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Datia in Claim Case No. 553/2021; whereby, appellant has been awarded a compensation of Rs. 7,04,768/- for the injuries sustained by him in road accident dated 12/1/2021.

entities.text: Second Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Datia
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Appellant has filed this appeal seeking enhancement in the compensation amount; whereas,
Insurance Company also filed cross objections under Order XLI Rule 22 of CPC assailing the quantum of compensation.

3. Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 12/1/2021 at about 7.30 pm when appellant was coming back to his home after Darshan of Hanuman Mandir, Sitasagar, it is alleged that as soon as he came out of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15791 2 MA-6431-2023 the temple, Car No.
MP32C1907 being driven by its driver in a very rash and negligent manner dashed him, due to which he sustained grievous injuries on whole of the body.
Therefore, he filed a claim case seeking total compesnation of Rs. 11,70,000/- however, by the impugned award, Claims Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs. 7,04,768/- alongwith interest.

4. It is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that learned Claims Tribunal erred in assessing the extent of disability at 10% whereas, as per the WCA, he suffered 14% permanent disability as his right leg thumb was amputated.

It is further submitted that the income of appellant Shivendra Pal vs Smt. Manju Shrivastav on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75611429/
1 as assessed at Rs. 7,000/- per month is on the lower side.

entities.text: Shivendra Pal vs Smt. Manju Shrivastav on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the amount awarded under the other head is also on lower side.

5. On the other hand, by filing cross-objections, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that the amount awarded towards earning loss due to permanent disability and towards loss of amenities and towards loss of marriage prospects and again towards loss of amenities are on the higher side and were not admissible in the present facts and circumstances of the case.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

Having gone through the record and impugned award, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal while assessing the incomes of appellant, assessing extent of permanent disablement and awarding amount under the other heads, appear to be after appreciation of evidence available on record and are just and proper and thus, in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15791 3 MA-6431-2023 opinion of this Court, amount awarded by the impugned award is just and proper.

Therefore, finding no merits in the appeal as well as cross- objections so preferred by Insurance Company, appeal as well as cross- objections both are hereby dismissed.
(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
